items.title: cPGuard Update Channel Hijacked to Backdoor Linux Servers and Collect Password Hashes
items.summary: An attacker broke into the update system of the cPGuard security tool on November 2 and used it to send a malicious script to customers' Linux servers. The script installed a backdoor and collected password hashes and other sensitive files from servers that ran it, cPGuard maker OPSSHIELD said in an advisory. The attacker has since taken some of that data. cPGuard 5.88.25 and later versions remove the backdoor and the files the script left. Credentials the script copied may still work after the update, so any server that may have run the script also needs new passwords and keys.

items.title: CWP2Shell: The Login Page That Never Says No
items.summary: Today VulnCheck is disclosing ten vulnerabilities in Control Web Panel (CWP, formerly CentOS Web Panel), the hosting control panel that ships on a large number of internet-facing servers. They are being disclosed in accordance with VulnCheck's coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy, and all ten carry allocated IDs through the VulnCheck CNA. The most severe of these is CVE-2026-73695, an unauthenticated remote code execution in the user panel of Control Web Panel. From that foothold the root-owned loopback user API gives two independent paths to root: its ungated routes (CVE-2026-77877) reach a command injection that runs as root, and a SQL injection in the API's authentication gate (CVE-2026-77879) forges past it to the same result. This was tested on the CWP7 webpanel 1.8 build on AlmaLinux 9, a build that already carries the patch for the last KEV-listed CWP RCE.

items.title: Russia-Aligned Gorbag Hackers Exploit WinRAR Flaw to Deploy Data-Stealing Malware
items.summary: A Russia-aligned threat actor known as Gorbag has been observed using simple information stealer malware in attacks targeting Ukrainian organizations. "Active since at least February 2025, the group has focused exclusively on Ukrainian targets, with a clear preference for law enforcement and justice entities, local administrations near the front line, and the defense sector," ESET researcher Damien Schaeffer said in a report shared with The Hacker News. The activity shares overlaps with a cluster tracked by the Computer Emergency Response Team of Ukraine (CERT-UA) under the moniker UAC-0226 and by Trend Micro as SHADOW-EARTH-066. Gorbag is known to be active since at least February 2025. A key tool in the threat actor's malware arsenal is GIFTEDCROOK, a C/C++ stealer that facilitates the theft of sensitive data from web browsers like Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Mozilla Firefox, such as cookies, browsing history, and authentication data.

items.title: Attackers Exploit Critical Siemens IoT2050 Flaw to Plant Remote Command Backdoors
items.summary: A maximum-severity security flaw impacting Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices has come under active exploitation, VulnCheck has revealed. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-58115 (CVSS score: 10.0), is a case of missing authentication for a critical function that could be exploited by an unauthenticated remote attacker to run arbitrary code. "SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed contain a missing authentication vulnerability in the Node-RED HTTP interface that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows and execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with maximum privileges," Siemens said in an advisory released back in August 2026.

items.title: Barracuda warns of critical flaws allowing root access to devices
items.summary: Cybersecurity company Barracuda Networks warned customers to patch two vulnerabilities that can let attackers run commands with root privileges. The first is a critical flaw (CVE-2026-116606) stemming from an Email Security Gateway (ESG) authentication weakness that attackers can exploit to modify an appliance's global configuration, while the second (CVE-2026-111560) lets threat actors with admin permissions inject OS commands that run as root. However, Barracuda said successful exploitation also requires access to the administrative interfaces of targeted devices and advised customers to use appropriate network access controls and restrict access to trusted internal networks to limit exposure.

items.title: Cyber chief: UK facing AI-powered attacks on critical infrastructure within two years
items.summary: The NCSC warns that ‘tech on the cheap’ has left UK organisations exposed to AI uncovering and exploiting longstanding cyber security weaknesses and calls for urgent investment in resilience. AI-powered malware highly likely to be used in ransomware attack on Britain’s critical national infrastructure by 2028, new report warns. Head of GCHQ’s National Cyber Security Centre to warn, as a society, the era of “tech on the cheap” at expense of security is over. New State of the Cyber Nation report calls on organisations to make “significant changes” to avert future where AI is used against UK economy and society.

items.title: What exploited vulnerabilities have in common: A data-driven analysis of real-world attacks
items.summary: The vulnerability landscape continues to expand. From 1999 through September 2026, approximately 383,000 software vulnerabilities had been disclosed across platforms and technologies, yet only about 2,000 CVEs (roughly 0.5%) have been linked to real-world exploitation. Those vulnerabilities follow clear patterns. Threat actors disproportionately target flaws that enable system takeover, particularly remote code execution, privilege escalation, and authentication bypass. AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploit development could further shorten the window defenders have to respond. Patching remains essential, but remediation can take weeks or months on critical systems, and some legacy or unsupported systems cannot be patched. Defenders therefore need to concentrate protection where it can have the greatest impact, considering both the likelihood of exploitation and the potential blast radius of a successful attack.

items.title: PHP2Shell: what we know about the threat two weeks later
items.summary: Late October brought several unsettling cybersecurity stories all at once. Among these were two critical vulnerabilities in PHP, which potentially affected about 70% of websites worldwide. CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 — dubbed PHP2Shell — could let attackers execute code on a server remotely, without authentication. On October 21, PHP’s developers released emergency patches for the supported PHP 8.2–8.5 branches and for the unsupported PHP 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1. Experts predicted that attacks on vulnerable servers would start within 15 minutes of the updates going public. Amazon even reported exploitation attempts four days before the patches came out. With all this in the news, some organizations sounded the alarm early. For example, in several countries, government service websites were taken offline as a precaution. Even Wikipedia’s project management and bug-tracking system suspended service. Nearly two weeks have passed since the updates came out, but according to Censys data, of the 46 million scannable servers running a vulnerable PHP version, 29 million still contain the flaws. Right after the patches were published, we broke down each flaw in detail and explained what companies and everyday users should do. In this post we cover what’s known about the threat today, and what extra steps businesses need to take.

items.title: Prompt Adware: How Hidden AI Instructions Could Create a New Enterprise Security Risk
items.summary: Check Point Research (CPR) discovered Haiou, an OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle that persistently modifies an AI agent’s trusted instructions to inject advertisements for a third-party AI gateway. CPR calls this behavior “prompt adware,” highlighting how natural-language prompts and configuration files can quietly influence an AI agent’s future behavior without traditional executable code. While the advertisement itself is relatively simple, the technique raises a broader concern for organizations adopting AI agents: how much visibility do they have into the third-party prompts, Skills and configurations influencing the AI systems they trust? Key Findings - CPR identified “prompt adware,” where trusted AI instructions are persistently modified through natural language to influence future outputs. - Haiou goes beyond jailbreaking Codex, modifying global agent instructions so common greetings trigger an advertisement for a third-party AI gateway. - The same persistence mechanism could enable less visible manipulation, including steering recommendations, promoting services or biasing technical advice without the user’s awareness. - The finding highlights a visibility challenge for AI adoption, as prompts, Skills and configurations become part of the broader ecosystem influencing agent behavior. - The potential business impact extends to confidential information, particularly if trusted third-party AI components are abused to perform malicious actions or exfiltrate sensitive data.

Check Point Research (CPR) discovered Haiou, an OpenAI Codex jailbreak bundle that persistently modifies an AI agent’s trusted instructions to inject advertisements for a third-party AI gateway. CPR calls this behavior “prompt adware,” highlighting how natural-language prompts and configuration files can quietly influence an AI agent’s future behavior without traditional executable code.

While the advertisement itself is relatively simple, the technique raises a broader concern for organizations adopting AI agents: how much visibility do they have into the third-party prompts, Skills and configurations influencing the AI systems they trust?

Key Findings

- CPR identified “prompt adware,” where trusted AI instructions are persistently modified through natural language to influence future outputs.

- Haiou goes beyond jailbreaking Codex, modifying global agent instructions so common greetings trigger an advertisement for a third-party AI gateway.

- The same persistence mechanism could enable less visible manipulation, including steering recommendations, promoting services or biasing technical advice without the user’s awareness.

- The finding highlights a visibility challenge for AI adoption, as prompts, Skills and configurations become part of the broader ecosystem influencing agent behavior.

- The potential business impact extends to confidential information, particularly if trusted third-party AI components are abused to perform malicious actions or exfiltrate sensitive data.
